reviewed: HB148 gives 37-inch carbon-steel operating levers and a gate formed by the two selectors. HB93 depicts lateral high/low selection; the handle and fulcrum are separate parts. Source lengths are not specified as centerline or pivot-to-tip measurements.

HB113 plan places M746/M747 inboard of the selector collars. Fulcrum collars belong to the main shaft, with a second handle pivot. Exact axial stations, second-pivot axis/offset and handle heel profile remain to be reconstructed.

Current selectors have radial end lips. A simple continuous radial stem in the nominal pocket necessarily crosses those lips; the previous empty-pocket check did not test a through-going operating handle. Tangential lips around a radial through-slot are the proposed interpretation of fore/aft actuation. Confirm it with complete handles and a source comparison before integration.

SNL23 original directly inspected: each M776 assembly includes M768 7/8-inch special nut and one 3/16 x 1-inch split pin. SNL129 original specifies crown, U.S. Std., 7/8 inch and 1/2-inch thickness for M767/M776. The generic SNL141 1-1/2-inch cotter row also names M776, so retain this conflict; do not silently lengthen a pin to fit an estimated crown.
SNL97 gives M747 left/port and M746 right/starboard; SNL117 gives M738B left and M738A right. Hardware and handle geometry are not yet accepted.
hypothesis: Reorient only selector upper jaws: keep journals and all lower connections intact. Use a 32 mm radial band and 70 mm tangential envelope, with estimated 12.7 mm lips. Existing high/low gate centers 175/250 mm and axial reaches remain estimates. No actual handle is represented by the diagnostic through-stem.
